feature_notes:
Improves usable scalar write performance: common values are converted before formula-class imports and structured-object checks. A one-million-numeric-cell write_only append/save on Linux CPython 3.12 improves from alpha.2 1.8726 s to alpha.3 1.4659 s (about 21.7% less time), with unchanged logical worksheet spool peak (32,866,902 bytes) and final ZIP size (2,942,935 bytes). Public readback verifies every value. See benchmarks/alpha3-writing.md for reproducible evidence and limits.

Pins published canonical Rust alpha.3 commit d9fddb01abf3da4715fa6f0cc7c00371d5826471. Bounded 64 KiB editor compression buffering reduces native million-cell A1 edit/save from 7.0485 s to 1.3450 s (5.24x), preserving byte-identical uncompressed package parts, formula-cache invalidation, original assets and failure cleanup. This native measurement excludes Python model loading and is not a full Python editing benchmark.

All 577 selected tests pass on each CPython 3.11 through 3.15 (currently RC) installed candidate wheel. Ruff format/check, Rustfmt and strict Clippy pass. Rust core MSRV remains 1.88; Python wheels use latest stable Rust.

Release builds share Rust dependencies within five platform/architecture jobs, each producing and testing all five Python ABIs: Linux x86_64/ARM64, Windows x86_64 and macOS Intel/Apple Silicon. The 25 wheels and independent sdist must pass before PyPI OIDC publication.

M2 and full baseline compatibility remain open. Optimized styles/rich objects, full structural editing, file-like I/O and advanced feature graphs remain staged. Worksheet spooling and atomic output ZIP storage are still required; memory component allowances are not an RSS cap.
